item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Optimizes SQLite C Extension Performance Beyond Rust Implementation
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 Optimizes SQLite C Extension Performance Beyond Rust Implementation

On November 8th, 2026, an investigation using the Claude Opus 5.5 model demonstrated the creation and optimization of a custom SQLite extension. The project focused on developing a parse_number() function to convert strings—such as currency and percentages—into numeric values that can be summed and sorted.

🔍 Overview

The parse_number(value) function was designed with specific parsing capabilities:

  • Strips symbols including ‘,’, ‘$’, ‘£’, and ‘%’.
  • Handles leading ‘-’ characters.
  • Returns ‘NULL’ for any values it cannot successfully parse.

⚙️ Key details

The development process compared building the extension in C versus Rust, revealing significant differences in file size and execution speed:

  • File Size: The C extension resulted in a 14 KB file, while Rust implementations were significantly larger at 321 KB (using Rusqlite) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs).
  • Performance Optimization: Although the Rust version was initially faster due to its strtod equivalent being twice as fast as C’s, a custom C function written by the AI achieved superior speeds.

📊 Performance results

The following table displays the net cost per row measured over 2 million rows. Lower values indicate better performance.

Data Type Original C New C Rusqlite (Rust) sqlite-loadable (Rust)
Mixed data 67 ns 19 ns 46 ns 41 ns
Integers only 25 ns 16 ns 36 ns 32 ns
Decimals only 106 ns 18 ns 55 ns 47 ns

🚀 Availability

The final prototype was formatted as a research report for the simonw/research GitHub repository. The model provided the investigation as a downloadable zip file containing the necessary folder structure for the repository.

#SQLite #ClaudeAI #Programming #Rust #C

Source: Research: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust

item.title: Comprehensive DevOps Engineer Roadmap: Tools, Languages, and Learning Path
item.description:
Comprehensive DevOps Engineer Roadmap: Tools, Languages, and Learning Path

A step‑by‑step DevOps engineer roadmap has been published to help newcomers navigate the vast DevOps landscape.

🗺️ Overview

  • The roadmap provides a complete DevOps learning guide and aims to give you an idea about the landscape.
  • It is designed to guide you when you are confused about what to learn next, rather than pushing hype or trendy topics.
  • The roadmap encourages understanding why one tool may be better suited for a case than another.

⚙️ Core Version‑Control Tool: Git

  • All resources (files) are held in a GIT repository.
  • Files include both application code and infrastructure‑as‑code.
  • Git is a free source‑code‑management tool that tracks changes and enables multiple developers to work together on non‑linear development.
  • Popular Git platforms mentioned are GitLab and GitHub.
  • Essential Git commands to learn: git clone, branch, merge, and collaborating with pull‑requests.

🖥️ Programming Foundations

  • As a DevOps engineer, you should know at least one programming language for automation scripts.
  • Popular languages for DevOps include Python, Go, and JavaScript.
  • Python details:
    • Multi‑paradigm language.
    • Interpreted: code executes immediately after writing.
    • Syntax permits writing code in various styles.
    • Frequently recommended as the first language for new coders because of readability, consistency, and ease of use.
  • Fundamental programming concepts to master: syntax, if/else, loops, data structures, etc.

🖥️ Operating System Basics

  • An operating system acts as a bridge between a computer’s user and its hardware.
  • Its function is to provide a setting where users can conveniently and effectively run programs.

📚 Learning Resources & Community

  • The roadmap includes links to relevant learning resources.
  • If you want to learn more about DevOps, you are encouraged to subscribe to the author’s newsletter.
  • Users can star the project if they find it helpful for learning or starting a solution.
  • Support options: consider supporting the author on Patreon or download the PDF version of the roadmap.

🚀 Next Steps

  • Follow the roadmap to plan your DevOps education path.
  • Start by setting up a Git repository, learning basic Git commands, and choosing a programming language (Python is a strong first choice).
  • Continue building knowledge of OS concepts and infrastructure‑as‑code tools as you progress.

#devops #git #python #programming #roadmap

Source: milanm/DevOps-Roadmap

item.title: Impact of Coding Agents on the Programming Profession
item.description:
Impact of Coding Agents on the Programming Profession

The emergence of coding agents is altering the nature of professional programming, specifically regarding the role of solving logic puzzles in software development.

💡 Why it matters

The shift toward LLMs impacts programmers differently based on their professional motivations:

  • For programmers who thrive on building working systems and do not care deeply about the problems solved along the way, LLMs are described as “the gift that keeps on giving.”
  • For programmers who enjoyed the puzzle of developing code, the loss is described as “very real.”

Historically, programming was characterized by the following:

  • Professionals were paid to work on “tricky little logic puzzles,” with higher pay for trickier puzzles.
  • Programmers set the strategy, defined the timeline, and determined what was and was not possible.
  • Regular people were unable to perform these tasks, making even simple puzzles valuable.

#LLMs #CodingAgents #Programming #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: My obituary for programming

item.title: Python 3.15 Released with Lazy Imports and New Sampling Profiler
item.description:
Python 3.15 Released with Lazy Imports and New Sampling Profiler

Python 3.15 has been released, introducing significant updates to import behavior, profiling tools, and language syntax. This release, curated by 3.14 and 3.15 release manager Hugo van Kemenade, focuses on reducing startup costs and improving system insights.

🧩 How it works

Python 3.15 introduces several functional improvements to the standard library and language core:

  • Explicit Lazy Imports (PEP 810): Modules can now be imported using lazy import json or lazy from pathlib import Path. The module is only imported the first time a symbol is used in the code. This feature directly addresses the startup cost of heavy dependencies; for instance, installing plugins using sentence_transformers can add seconds to command invocations without lazy loading.
  • Unpacking in Comprehensions (PEP 798): A new syntax [*sublist for sublist in lists] allows for unpacking within comprehensions. Proposed by Adam Hartz and Erik Demaine, this is an extension of the unpacking syntax introduced in PEP 448.
  • Tachyon Sampling Profiler: A new sampling profiler called Tachyon (available as profiling.sampling) joins the standard library. Unlike tracing profilers, it periodically captures stack traces from running processes, allowing for low-overhead insights into running systems. Users can attach it to an existing process via its PID, such as using sudo uv run --python 3.15 python -m profiling.sampling attach 1234.

⚙️ Key details

The release includes several updates to the SQLite module and existing utilities:

Feature Description
profiling.tracing The new name for the existing cProfile tracing profiler.
blobopen() Efficient mechanism for partial reads and writes of large SQLite BLOB binary values.
create_window_function() Allows creating custom SQLite window functions using a class with step, value, inverse, and finalize methods.
setlimit() / getlimit() Exposes a mechanism for setting SQLite runtime limits from Python.
set_authorizer(None) Provides a method to remove an existing SQLite authorizer.
datetime.UTC An alias for datetime.timezone.utc (originally introduced in 3.11).

🔍 Overview

Performance testing of the 3.15.0rc3 release by Miguel Grinberg shows that speed remains mostly consistent with Python 3.14. However, the experimental JIT demonstrated a 1.2x boost over the standard interpreter in a Fibonacci test, marking a meaningful performance increase for the JIT.

With the arrival of Python 3.15, Python 3.10 (released in 2021) is officially no longer supported. The Tachyon profiler also introduces advanced visualization capabilities, including the ability to produce flame graphs, heat maps, and formats compatible with the Firefox profiler UI.

#Python #Programming #SoftwareDevelopment #Python315

Source: Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11

item.title: Anthropic Updates Claude Code with Performance Optimizations and Specialized Agent Skills
item.description:
Anthropic Updates Claude Code with Performance Optimizations and Specialized Agent Skills

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in the terminal, providing developers with the ability to understand codebases, explain complex logic, and handle git workflows through natural language. The tool has received updates focused on performance optimization, specialized creative skills, and secure execution environments.

🔍 Overview

Claude Code is designed to execute routine tasks and manage codebases with an approach where “the best code is the code you never wrote.” The system is built to make AI agents operate with high efficiency, similar to an experienced senior developer.

  • Terminal-based Operation: Lives directly in the command line for seamless workflow integration.
  • Codebase Understanding: Analyzes and explains complex code structures.
  • Task Execution: Handles routine development tasks and git operations using natural language commands.
  • Core Development: Features a research-first approach incorporating skills, instincts, memory, and security.

⚙️ Key details

The development of Claude Code and related agents now includes specialized skills for both quality control and content production.

  • Taste-Skill: This feature gives the AI “good taste,” stopping it from generating boring or generic content.
  • AI Video Skill: Designed for Claude Code and Codex, this skill enables the creation of cinematic product videos using Remotion. It includes a production-ready template, 152 shot recipe cards, and 209 motion previews.
  • Agent Harness: A performance optimization system designed for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, and Cursor.

🧩 How it works

The system utilizes a hybrid architecture to ensure precise code analysis and secure execution.

  • Hybrid Code Review: Combines deterministic pipelines with LLM Agents to deliver precise, line-level comments. It includes built-in rulesets for multiple languages to detect Null Pointer Exceptions (NPE), thread-safety issues, XSS, and SQL injection.
  • OpenShell Runtime: Provides a safe and private runtime environment specifically for autonomous AI agents.
  • Model Compatibility: Supports cross-converting various models into OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini-compatible formats through a unified hub.

🛠️ Infrastructure and Access

Component Description
OpenClaw An agent-first Identity and Access Management (IAM) and auth server supporting OAuth, OIDC, and MFA.
Sub2API A unified open-source service for accessing Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, and Grok subscriptions.
OpenShell A safe, private runtime environment for autonomous agents.
OpenClaw Gateway Supports integration with Google Workspace, Azure AD, and various authentication methods like Face ID.

#ClaudeCode #AIAgents #SoftwareDevelopment #Programming

Source: LLM News

item.title: Python 3.15 Introduces Soft Deprecation for re.match()
item.description:
Python 3.15 Introduces Soft Deprecation for re.match()

Python 3.15 is introducing the soft deprecation of the re.match() function, marking it as an API that should no longer be used to write new code without a promise or threat of future removal.

⚙️ Key details

Python 3.15 release manager Hugo van Kemenade describes the move to soft deprecate the “venerable but deeply confusing” re.match() function. A clearer alternative has been introduced to reflect how the function anchors at the beginning of a string, but not the end.

🧩 How it works

Depending on the desired outcome, developers can use the following functions:

Function Purpose
re.prefixmatch() The clearer alternative to re.match()
re.search() Match a pattern anywhere in the string
re.fullmatch() Match the entire string

#Python #Programming #SoftwareDevelopment #Python315

Source: Soft-deprecating re.match()
